html:
SMTO-RST-0012 — These details are no longer saved

GUID: 5a476ccf-cdc2-42a2-8c1f-67633aa861ce
Slug: retained-payload-missing
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • You tried to open or copy extra details for a step, such as a command's output, but SMTO no longer has them stored. The task's own result is not affected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close this panel and read the task's summary and final answer in the conversation to see what the step did. The summary is kept even when the detailed output for a single step is gone.
  2. Refresh the page and open the step again, in case the conversation view was out of date. If the task was still updating, the details may appear once the page shows its latest state.
  3. If you need to know the current state, check the file or system directly, or ask SMTO in a new message to look at it without changing anything. Looking at the current state is safe, while running the original step again could repeat its changes.
  4. If details are often missing for older tasks, ask the person who manages SMTO whether the automatic clean-up options in Settings › Data are removing them. Automatic clean-up can remove older tasks and their saved details.

What success looks like

  • You can see what the step did from its summary, or the details open after refreshing.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO if you expected these details to still be there. Don't re-run the task only to rebuild its output.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A trace detail lookup found no retained record: the activity detail, raw payload reference or captured Shell command (operation start event) is absent from this request's trace.

What this means

  • Raw payload/activity/command lookup cannot find the requested retained detail or cannot correlate the shell operation to a recorded start event. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Raw payload/activity/command lookup cannot find the requested retained detail or cannot correlate the shell operation to a recorded start event.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact request/operation identity with retained summaries and receipts; missing detail is separate from execution outcome.

How to fix it

  • Check the trace for the request: get_activity_detail, get_raw_payload and the native RunStore entry for the data ref, or the shell_command operation start for the operation_id. If the detail was purged or never recorded, use the trace summary and receipts or inspect current state; do not replay completed work to recreate diagnostics.
  • Open the retained trace summary and receipts. If detailed payload retention expired, use current-state inspection; do not replay completed work to reconstruct diagnostics.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Available evidence is accessed through current references and any unavailable detail remains disclosed.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
